title: Extension Interfaces: CNI, CSI, CRI
summary: How the kubelet plugs in container runtimes (CRI), Pod networking (CNI), storage (CSI) and special hardware (device plugins).

blocks.text: Customising a cluster is either **configuration** (flags, config files, API resources) or an **extension** (extra programs or services). You rarely need to fork Kubernetes.

items: **Webhook model:** Kubernetes calls a remote service over the network.
**Binary plugin model:** Kubernetes runs a program. The kubelet uses this for **CNI** network plugins and **CSI** storage plugins.
A **controller** is an API client that reads an object's `.spec`, acts, then updates its `.status`.

blocks.text: FlexVolume storage plugins are **deprecated since v1.23** in favour of CSI.

The **CRI** is the main **gRPC** protocol between the kubelet and the container runtime. It lets the kubelet use many runtimes without recompiling cluster components. Every node needs a working runtime so the kubelet can start Pods.

items: The kubelet is the gRPC **client**; the runtime serves the runtime and image service endpoints.
Point the kubelet at the runtime with the `--container-runtime-endpoint` flag.
Since **v1.26** the kubelet needs a runtime that supports the **v1 CRI API**. If it doesn't, the kubelet won't register the node.

blocks.text: After a node upgrade, if the kubelet fails to register, check that the container runtime supports CRI v1. Once the runtime is fixed, you may need to restart the kubelet.

A **CNI** (Container Network Interface) plugin is required to implement the Kubernetes network model. Use one compatible with CNI spec **v0.4.0 or later**; the project recommends one compatible with **v1.0.0**.

items: The **container runtime** loads the CNI plugins, not the kubelet. The kubelet flags `cni-bin-dir` and `network-plugin` were removed in **1.24**.
Runtimes must also provide a loopback interface `lo` for each sandbox; the CNI loopback plugin can do this.
`hostPort` support comes from the `portmap` plugin with the `portMappings` capability.
Traffic shaping uses the `bandwidth` plugin plus the `kubernetes.io/ingress-bandwidth` and `kubernetes.io/egress-bandwidth` Pod annotations.

blocks.text: **CSI** (Container Storage Interface) is a standard way for orchestrators to expose any storage system to containers. Once a CSI driver is deployed, you use the `csi` volume type.

items: Ways to use a CSI volume in a Pod: through a **PersistentVolumeClaim**, a **generic ephemeral volume**, or a **CSI ephemeral volume** (if the driver supports it).
**CSI migration** sends operations for in-tree plugins to the matching CSI driver, so existing StorageClasses, PVs and PVCs need no changes. You still have to install that driver yourself.
FlexVolume is deprecated; out-of-tree CSI drivers are the recommended way to add external storage.

blocks.text: Device plugins advertise hardware such as **GPUs, NICs and FPGAs** to the kubelet, so vendors don't change Kubernetes code. Deploy one as a **DaemonSet**, as an OS package, or by hand.

items: The plugin serves gRPC on a Unix socket under `/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/` and registers through `/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/kubelet.sock`.
Resource names use `vendor-domain/resourcetype`, for example `nvidia.com/gpu`. The kubelet reports the devices in the node status.
Extended resources are **integers only**, cannot be overcommitted, and a device is **not shared** between containers.
The device directory needs privileged access, so the plugin runs privileged. As a DaemonSet, mount that directory as a volume.
When the kubelet restarts it deletes the sockets; plugins must re-register.
An unhealthy device lowers the node's **allocatable** count; **capacity** stays the same.

flashcards.front: What protocol does the kubelet use to talk to the container runtime?
flashcards.back: The CRI, a gRPC protocol. The kubelet is the client.

flashcards.front: Kubelet flag that sets the container runtime endpoint?
Since v1.26, what happens if the runtime lacks the v1 CRI API?
flashcards.back: The kubelet won't register the node.

flashcards.front: Who loads CNI plugins since Kubernetes 1.24?
flashcards.back: The container runtime. The kubelet flags cni-bin-dir and network-plugin were removed.

flashcards.front: Minimum CNI spec version supported? Recommended?
flashcards.back: v0.4.0 or later; v1.0.0 is recommended.

flashcards.front: Default CNI config dir and binary dir?
Which CNI plugin provides hostPort support?
Three ways a Pod can use a CSI volume?
flashcards.back: Via a PVC, a generic ephemeral volume, or a CSI ephemeral volume.

flashcards.front: Which CSI PV field uniquely identifies the volume?

flashcards.back: Deprecated since v1.23; use a CSI driver instead.

flashcards.front: Which kubelet plugins use the binary (exec) model?
flashcards.back: CNI network plugins and CSI storage plugins.

flashcards.front: Where does a device plugin register with the kubelet?
Can two containers share one device from a device plugin?
flashcards.back: No. Devices can't be shared, and extended resources can't be overcommitted.

flashcards.front: Common way to deploy a device plugin?
flashcards.back: As a DaemonSet (also possible as an OS package or manually).
